newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal parliament to begin no-confidence debate.
newsitem.headline: Nepal parliament to begin no-confidence debate.

text.p: Nepal's parliament was to meet in special session on Monday to consider a communist-backed no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba's government.
The United Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, backed by renegade members of a party in Deuba's coalition, registered the motion against the 15-month-old government last Wednesday.
Under the Himalayan kingdom's five-year-old constitution, a vote on the motion cannot be held until at least 10 days after the date it is registered.
Debate on the motion was set to start later on Monday and a vote was expected next week.
The communists were bolstered by a breakaway faction of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), one of three partners in Deuba's tenuous governing coalition.

Eleven rebel RPP deputies announced last week that they were withdrawing support for Deuba's coalition, which had controlled 108 seats in the 205-seat lower house. Deuba's centrist Nepali Congress party has 86 lawmakers. The RPP, considered close to the monarchy, has 19 seats and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP) three.
To topple Deuba, the opposition would need at least 103 votes as Nepal's constitution requires the motion be passed by a majority of the 205-member house.
The opposition claims the support of at least 102 members -- the UML's 87 deputies, two independents, the 11 rebel RPP deputies and two NSP lawmakers.
The Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party (NWPP), a small left-wing group which has three members and potentially holds the swing votes, has not yet committed itself.
The government has disputed the opposition's claim that it has enough votes to topple Deuba.
The communists won general elections in 1994 and governed until the three opposition parties toppled the minority government and formed a ruling coalition in September 1995.
The rebel RPP deputies have accused the Nepali Congress of harassing their activists and breaking unspecified promises.
